stem:
Arnav compares tomatoes grown on a nearby farm with the same kind of tomatoes brought from far away.

Which claims about food miles are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: The nearby tomatoes travel a shorter distance from farm to plate, so they have fewer food miles.
Fewer food miles can mean less fuel on the journey, which can lower transport cost and pollution.
Tomatoes grown nearby always have fewer food miles, even if they travel through a distant warehouse first.
Putting the same tomatoes on sale reduces their food miles even when the delivery route stays unchanged.

teacher.key_rationale: Local food has fewer food miles when the route from farm to plate is shorter; that can cut transport fuel, cost, and pollution. A distant warehouse still adds miles, and a sale does not shorten the route.
